div.div:
Minimum 2 worker nodes, at least 2 vCPU and 4 GiB each. One per zone is the documented best practice. The gateway is stateless, so it scales horizontally.
Workload Identity binds the Kubernetes ServiceAccount to a Google service account, which is how the pods reach Cloud Storage with no static key. Installed with helm install portkey-ai/gateway into namespace portkeyai.

div.div: 9 Inbound: management plane to gateway, over Private Service Connect or an IP allow-list

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 809px; margin-left: 3px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: Traffic crosses the VPC boundary in both directions. Flows 6, 8, and 9 reach Palo Alto Networks, and none of them carries prompt or completion content. Flow 4 is where that content lands, inside your own account. Configure both directions: outbound alone leaves a gateway that serves traffic but never appears in Strata Cloud Manager.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 837px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-style: italic; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: Create the REGIONAL_MANAGED_PROXY subnet before you deploy. It is a prerequisite of the VPC rather than the chart, so nothing in the Helm output will tell you it is missing. The symptom is a load balancer that never provisions.
